meta.preliminaryPhases: The substance and phase association is a preliminary editorial assignment. Atlas educational phases are not a personal clinical timeline.

assessment.title: Advice before cutting down on alcohol
assessment.body: If physical alcohol dependence may be present, seek medical advice before abruptly cutting down or stopping. A sudden drop in intake can cause severe withdrawal in dependent drinkers.

emergency.title: Intense symptoms during alcohol withdrawal
emergency.body: Seizures, severe confusion, or disorientation during possible alcohol withdrawal require immediate medical attention.

nutrition.title: Vitamin B1 and alcohol use
nutrition.body: Harmful alcohol use may be associated with vitamin B1 deficiency. A healthcare professional can assess whether thiamine is needed.

emergency.title: Severe alcohol intoxication
emergency.body: Loss of consciousness, slow or irregular breathing, or seizures after drinking may be signs of alcohol overdose. If you suspect it, call emergency services; do not wait for every symptom to appear.

sedatives.title: Alcohol and sedative medicines
sedatives.body: Combining alcohol with benzodiazepines, opioids, or hypnotic sleeping medicines increases the risk of profound sedation and breathing problems.

support.title: Support for stopping tobacco
support.body: Behavioral counseling and tobacco cessation treatments can improve the chances of quitting. Ask about available options.

triggers.title: Nicotine use triggers
triggers.body: The urge to smoke is often tied to people, places, or habits. Noticing those triggers and having another activity ready (distraction or keeping busy) may help.

cravings.title: Managing nicotine cravings
cravings.body: When the urge to smoke arises, try distracting yourself, taking a walk, or texting or calling someone you trust. The urge can pass without smoking.

sleep.title: Sleep during nicotine withdrawal
sleep.body: After quitting smoking, a regular sleep schedule and avoiding caffeine in the afternoon or evening may help: caffeine can last longer in the body after you stop smoking.

mood.title: Mood changes when stopping nicotine
mood.body: Irritability is common after quitting smoking. If mood changes are severe, persistent, or interfere with daily activities, seek advice from a healthcare professional.

symptoms.title: Symptoms when reducing cannabis
symptoms.body: Reducing or stopping frequent cannabis use may cause irritability, anxiety, sleep problems, and appetite changes. Do not automatically attribute every symptom to withdrawal.

sleep.title: Sleep during cannabis withdrawal
sleep.body: Vivid or unusual dreams and sleep difficulties may occur during cannabis withdrawal. If the problem persists, seek assessment.

mood.title: Mood during cannabis withdrawal
mood.body: Seek professional assessment if significant mood changes, intense anxiety, or difficulty functioning occur.

support.title: Psychological support for cannabis use
support.body: If reducing or stopping cannabis is difficult, psychological interventions such as behavioral therapies may help. Ask about options; they are not a personal guarantee.

support.title: Cannabis and psychological symptoms
support.body: Seek healthcare support if cannabis use coincides with concerning psychological symptoms or with worsening of existing problems. That alone does not prove the cause.

chest_pain.title: Chest pain and cocaine
chest_pain.body: Chest pain during or after cocaine use requires urgent medical assessment. Age does not make it less important.

neurological.title: Neurological symptoms and cocaine
neurological.body: Seizures or loss of consciousness after cocaine use require emergency care. Sudden weakness, trouble speaking, or severe confusion also require emergency care.

interaction.title: Mixing cocaine and alcohol
interaction.body: Combining cocaine and alcohol may increase cardiovascular risks, including some serious outcomes. Avoid using them together.

behavioral_support.title: Behavioral support for stimulant use
behavioral_support.body: Clinical guidelines include behavioral interventions for stimulant use disorder, including contingency management. Ask about specialized programs. No program guarantees an individual outcome.

mood.title: Mood after stopping cocaine
mood.body: If very low mood or thoughts of self-harm occur after stopping cocaine, seek professional help now. If there is immediate danger, call emergency services. Do not wait for a calendar phase.

sensitivity.title: Individual caffeine tolerance
sensitivity.body: Caffeine tolerance varies between individuals. The FDA's 400 mg daily reference for most adults is neither a target nor a guarantee of individual safety.

gradual_reduction.title: Cutting back on caffeine gradually
gradual_reduction.body: If you regularly consume caffeine and want to cut back, reducing it gradually may help you avoid discomfort associated with stopping suddenly.

headache.title: Discomfort when stopping caffeine
headache.body: If you stop caffeine suddenly, headaches, drowsiness, and irritability can occur. Do not assume severe or unusual symptoms are caused solely by withdrawal.

anxiety.title: Caffeine, sleep, and anxiety
anxiety.body: If caffeine worsens your sleep or anxiety, consider cutting back. Effects can last several hours, so avoid it late in the day.

interactions.title: Caffeine and other treatments
interactions.body: Certain medicines and medical conditions may affect caffeine-related risks. Ask a healthcare professional if you are concerned about interactions.
